accounting issues, and lead the implementation of new accounting pronouncements that affect disclosures.</li> <li>Maintain Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) requirements for relevant areas, support internal and external reporting packages, and lead or contribute to special projects such as process improvements, new disclosure requirements, and merger and acquisition reporting.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>A bachelor’s degree in Accounting.</li> <li>Certified Public Accountant (CPA) licensure or active pursuit of licensure is preferred.</li> <li>Experience in owning SEC reporting deliverables, including Forms 10-K and 10-Q, in a public company or a public accounting environment serving public company clients.</li> <li>A record of improving disclosures and reporting processes, not only executing existing processes.</li> <li>Strong project management skills, with the ability to own a calendar, drive accountability across teams, and manage competing deadlines independently.</li> <li>Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to research and interpret complex accounting guidance.</li> <li>Clear written and verbal communication skills, with experience presenting to and influencing senior stakeholders and collaborating with Legal, FP&A, Investor Relations, and business partners.</li> <li>Proficiency with Workiva Wdesk and NetSuite is preferred.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>The Accounting team supports accurate, timely, and transparent financial reporting at GitLab. In this role, you’ll work closely with partners across Accounting, Legal, FP&A, and Investor Relations to meet public company reporting requirements and strengthen the processes and controls behind our disclosures. technical presentation and communication skills, with the ability to engage both technical and business stakeholders.</li> <li value="5">Knowledge of the end-to-end software development lifecycle, <li value="7">Familiarity with cloud computing concepts, related technologies, and common customer adoption patterns.</li> <li value="8">Ability and willingness to travel in line with business needs and the company's travel policy, and openness to learning and using GitLab and related tools, including through transferable experience from adjacent domains.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The rules.</li> <li>Apply infrastructure as code and configuration as code practices to interact with and validate existing GitLab Dedicated environments.</li> <li>Advise customers on migration sequencing, cutover windows, integration requirements, risks, and clear next steps.</li> <li>Improve migration tooling, scripts, and runbooks to make delivery more reliable, repeatable, and efficient.</li> <li>Partner with Professional Services, Environment Automation, Product, and Engineering to resolve blockers, share field feedback, and keep delivery consistent.</li> <li>Manage multiple customer engagements while balancing customer outcomes, delivery priorities, and share technical knowledge with other engineers.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> running Kubernetes workloads in production, including deployments, rollouts, and debugging crash loops, failed health checks, and scheduling issues.</li> <li>Experience with a major cloud provider infrastructure tooling, with familiarity in languages such as Go, Python, or Ruby.</li> <li>Ability to independently lead multiple customer projects, communicate clearly in written and spoken English, description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>About the role</strong></h2> <p>We are looking for a Principal Engineer to help build GitLab Duo Agent Platform, the agentic orchestration layer that runs AI agents and flows across the entire software lifecycle.</p> <p>Principal Engineers at GitLab are recognized experts across multiple technology domains and represent the senior technical leadership within their organization. In this role you will set technical direction for a significant part of the Agent Platform, working across several teams to turn agentic capabilities into something engineering organizations can actually depend on: predictable, observable, governable, and fast enough to sit in the critical path of real development work.</p> <p>The Agent Platform is not a single service. It spans agent execution and orchestration, flow definition and event-driven triggering, the AI Catalog through which customers discover and manage agents, model routing and evaluation, and the governance surface that decides which agents may act where and under whose identity. It runs on GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, and Self-Managed installations, including deployments that use self-hosted models to meet compliance requirements. You will work on the parts of that system where the hard architectural questions live, and you will do it hands-on.</p> <p>This role reports into the VP of the AI Engineering organization and works closely with Engineering Managers, Staff Engineers, Product Management, Infrastructure and Security.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Define the technical direction for a significant area of Duo Agent Platform across several teams, and partner with Engineering Managers and Product to turn it into a roadmap with a six-month horizon.</li> <li>Build the orchestration layer that makes agents and flows reliable: session lifecycle, tool invocation, context assembly, concurrency, retries, timeouts, and failure modes that degrade gracefully instead of stalling a developer's workflow.</li> <li>Hands on work on driving topics throughout the whole organisation from POC level, architecture to full implementation. </li> <li>Participate in Incident Management on-call rotation, to help meet availability goals for GitLab.com.</li> <li>Strong product builder and ownership mentality. Understanding of product strategy, technical strategy, delivering customer value and iteration towards a successful product</li> <li>Write clear, opinionated design documents, architecture narratives, and decision records that let other teams make aligned decisions. Ensure the architecture holds across multi-tenant GitLab.com, Dedicated, and Self-Managed deployments, including self-hosted model configurations, and respects data governance boundaries in each.</li> <li>Use the platform on our own work, find where it falls short of what we claim, and feed that back through improvements into the product.</li> <li>Mentor Staff and Senior Engineers, and raise the bar for experimentation rigor and cross-team collaboration.</li> <li>Work across the whole platform on different projects, features and teams. title: Principal Program Manager, Go-To-Market
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><p>GitLab is an open-core software company that develops the <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/platform/">intelligent orchestration platform</a> for DevSecOps, used by more than 100,000 organizations and 50 million people. Our mission is to unlock every team to ship trusted software at the speed of imagination.</p> <p>Software is increasingly built by machines and directed by people. When agentic coding tools accelerate without context, governance, and lifecycle control, teams get speed with chaos. GitLab enables speed with control: customers deploy agents across the software development lifecycle (SDLC) with the orchestration, context, security, and governance to ship trusted software at scale.</p> <p>The same principles show up in how we work. We build a culture of excellence around Speed with Quality, Ownership Mindset, and Customer Outcomes, and we treat AI as a core productivity multiplier. Every team member is expected to put AI into daily workflows to move faster without losing control. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued.</p> <h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As Principal Program Manager, Go-To-Market, you own two equal pillars of go-to-market execution for Product & Technical Marketing (PTM). First, you are the strategic and hands-on architect behind GitLab's high-stakes minor and major launches, redesigning the launch operating model with AI agents at its core so customers discover, adopt, and experience GitLab with precision. </p> <p>Second, you run program management on key initiatives that span Product Management and Product Design through Growth Marketing, Comms and Social, and Field Enablement, wherever those motions depend on PTM. PTM team  is responsible for product and solutions marketing, technical writing and documentation, developer advocacy, and globalization, and acts as the glue between these functions across a variety of go-to-market initiatives.</p> <p>You are AI-first by default. When programs still run on many manual steps, you convert that work into team-wide AI workflows, either by shipping the automations yourself or by partnering with the AI Transformation Owner (ATO) for the marketing organization to drive shared skills, adoption, and governance. You are not a reactive deadline chaser. You drive solutions with stakeholders as dates approach, design decision stages so tradeoffs land early, and redesign stages and workflows when product roadmap, growth priorities, or major launch decisions change. You create clarity in ambiguity: frame the problem, present options and tradeoffs, name owners, and optimize for decision velocity.</p> <p>In your first year, you institutionalize a dual operating system: a scalable launch framework for 15+ minor and major launches per year, and a portfolio program practice that maps dependencies from Product and Design through PTM into Growth, Comms, and Field. You ship production agent workflows that cut manual coordination, establish benchmarks for quality, and make go-to-market program management achieve relevance in the AI era, and become a trusted partner across the organization. </p> <p>Reporting to the VP of Product & Technical Marketing, you operate with significant executive visibility and autonomy. You measure success by what lands for customers and the business: pipeline where it matters, and brand and community impact where business requires it, not by activity volume alone.</p> <h2><strong>Some examples of projects:</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Orchestrate minor launches that put new platform releases in front of the community</li> <li>Orchestrate major launches tied to company events that move pipeline</li> <li>Orchestrate weekly signal announcements so we stay present in a fast-moving ecosystem</li> <li>Sequence product decisions into PTM and other go-to-market functions, with clear handoffs</li> <li>Keep field enablement on track when they depend on messaging and sales assets</li> <li>Design decision points early so blockers show up before the deadline</li> <li>Scope launches for pipeline and for post-launch adoption when agentic products are involved</li> <li>Build AI workflows that draft briefs, synthesize status, and cut manual program steps</li> <li>Rebuild stages and calendars when roadmap, growth priorities, or launch plans change</li> <li>Run retrospectives that improve the system, and remove process as often as you add it</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Run a concurrent portfolio of PTM-dependent initiatives with clear owners, dates, and tradeoffs</li> <li>Give leadership the context to decide: risks, options, and a recommendation, not status theater</li> <li>Align go-to-market functions when work streams collide or compete for the same people</li> <li>Codify how programs run so each cycle starts sharper than the last</li> <li>Put quality in the path of the work, then confirm market-facing pieces landed as intended</li> <li>Turn recurring coordination into shared AI workflows the team can run without you in the loop</li> <li>Partner with Marketing's ATO when a workflow needs department-wide adoption or guardrails</li> <li>Escalate early with a clear ask when a call sits above the working team</li> <li>Protect focus with smaller core teams, fewer standing meetings, more working sessions</li> <li>Close the loop on results with the data team, then feed what you learn into the next cycle</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Program management for go-to-market across the high-tech industry, with first-hand experience with complex, multi-stakeholder and cross-functional initiatives.</li> <li>Experience building and scaling how programs run in large, distributed orgs, with clear results </li> <li>Hands-on work with AI agents and automations that real teams used in production</li> <li>A track record of turning manual work into AI workflows and helping others adopt them</li> <li>Comfort standing up launch and program frameworks without adding busywork</li> <li>Strong grasp of how product releases and how they impact go-to-market teams</li> <li>Bias to action for priorities: defining risks and clear options for path forward</li> <li>Habit of measuring success by pipeline, adoption, or consumption, not activity counts</li> <li>Ability to run several high-stakes workstreams at once without dropping quality or trust</li> <li>Clear writing and speaking with executives; gets decisions made across competing priorities</li> <li>Influence without direct authority, including with senior leaders</li> <li>Fluency with project tools with AI automation on top, and the ability to use GitLab</li> <li>Ability to travel if needed and comply with the company's travel policy</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>Product & Technical Marketing at GitLab is the engine behind how GitLab positions, launches, documents, and evangelizes its value proposition for enterprises worldwide. We connect GitLab's product capabilities to customers and prospects across technical personas and executive buyers, and we partner closely with Product Management, Product Design, Growth Marketing, Comms and Social, Field Enablement, Sales, and the broader go-to-market organization so what we build lands in market with clarity, impact, and relevance. We operate as one marketing organization with clear roles: PTM carries the message; Growth activates demand; Comms amplifies narrative; work moves when handoffs are explicit.</p> <p>You serve as the senior operational and program spine inside Product & Technical Marketing. You translate roadmap and positioning strategy into coordinated launches and PTM-dependent initiatives across the go-to-market chain, while building the playbooks and AI-powered workflows that make excellence repeatable at scale. We are building towards an operational model where agents handle the scaffolding of cross-functional programs, freeing team members to focus on strategy and judgement.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. the Senior Manager of Application Security.</p> <h4><strong>What you'll do </strong></h4> <ul> <li>Conduct and lead security research projects across multiple functional areas.</li> <li>Identify novel, systemic, and chained vulnerabilities in GitLab, where individual weaknesses combine for outsized impact.</li> <li>Validate security vulnerabilities through hands-on testing, developing proof-of-concept exploits that demonstrate real-world attack scenarios.</li> <li>Assess emerging industry vulnerability classes against the GitLab codebase, and drive remediation of the class rather than the instance.</li> <li>Lead security research into GitLab's AI and agentic surfaces, and define the security requirements that engineering teams build against.</li> <li>Build and direct the tooling and automation that scales security research, including agent-assisted vulnerability discovery across our codebase.</li> <li>Research the security posture of open source tools and dependencies integrated with GitLab, report findings to their maintainers, and track mitigation following our <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/security/disclosure/">responsible disclosure guidelines</a>.</li> the engineering and business functions that need to act on them.</li> <li>Teach, mentor, and advise other domain experts and individual contributors across several teams.</li> <li>Share knowledge and novel vulnerability types with the security community.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h4> <ul> <li>10+ years of experience in security research, penetration testing, or offensive security roles</li> <li>Strong ability in discovering and exploiting vulnerabilities in large codebase and complex systems</li> <li>Proficiency in two or more of Ruby, Go, Python, TypeScript, or Rust. </li> <li>Ability to read and analyze code across multiple languages and codebases</li> <li>Strong knowledge of AI frameworks</li> <li>Strong understanding of AI attack vectors including prompt injection, agent manipulation, and workflow exploitation</li> <li>At ease in establishing and driving complex remediation initiatives involving cross-functional teams</li> <li>Excellent written communication skills with an ability to articulate complex topics in a clear and concise manner.</li> <li>Ability to translate complex technical findings into clear risk assessments and remediation recommendations</li> <li>Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with creative thinking about attack scenarios</li> <li><strong>Nice to Have: </strong>Published security research or conference presentations; background in software engineering with distributed systems expertise; experience with GitLab or similar DevSecOps platforms</li> </ul> <h4><strong>About the team</strong></h4> <p>Security Researchers are a part of our<a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/security/product-security/security-platforms-architecture/"> </a>Application Security team, who address complex security challenges facing GitLab and its customers to enable GitLab to be the most secure software factory platform on the market. You'll provide DevOps and DevSecOps consulting and best practices, contribute reusable collateral such as documentation, delivery kits, and training materials, and share product release updates to help the team deliver consistent outcomes. This role combines deep technical expertise with customer-facing leadership in GitLab's remote, asynchronous, and values-driven environment.</p> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <ul> <li>Designing and delivering GitLab reference architecture implementations for both self-managed and cloud environments, using infrastructure as code practices.</li> <li>Leading source code management and CI/CD migrations to GitLab, including large-scale enterprise moves using Congregate.</li> <li>Building repeatable delivery kits, documentation, and enablement materials that help Professional Services and partners deploy and adopt GitLab best practices.</li> <li>Lead the full technical delivery lifecycle for GitLab Professional Services engagements, from early scoping and technical discovery through implementation and handoff.</li> <li>Produce high-level and detailed technical designs for GitLab infrastructure and functionality, ensuring deliverables align with customer requirements and expectations.</li> <li>Evaluate and communicate scalability and security considerations (including compliance constraints) in proposed GitLab reference architectures and implementation plans.</li> <li>Deploy and configure GitLab in customer environments, including on-premises and major cloud providers, using Terraform, Ansible, and the GitLab Environment Toolkit (GET) aligned to reference architectures.</li> <li>Plan and execute source system migrations to GitLab using Congregate, partnering closely with customer stakeholders to reduce risk, protect data integrity, and minimize downtime.</li> <li>Provide DevOps and DevSecOps consulting and best-practice guidance, including advising on internal frameworks such as the Delivery Governance Framework (DGF) and GitLab Flow.</li> <li>Coordinate and oversee implementation work across GitLab team members, partners, and customer points of contact (POCs), ensuring clear asynchronous communication and decision capture, effective execution, and high-quality outcomes.</li> <li>Mentor Professional Services and partner consultants by contributing documentation, delivery kits, and training materials, and by leading enablement sessions on how to deliver and position service offerings.</li> <li>Maintain and improve delivery automation assets with an emphasis on code cleanliness, maintainability, and appropriate unit/integration testing.</li> <li>Support scoping and Statement of Work (SOW) creation with Professional Services Engagement Managers, stay current on monthly GitLab releases, and help Regional Delivery Managers with technical vetting and staffing assessments while maintaining a 55% billable utilization.</li> <li>Review and provide input to Professional Services training materials and presentations.</li> <li>Develop case studies, presentations, design documentation, and best-practice methodologies.</li> <li>Work closely with customer project teams to ensure accurate task-level articulation of work required.</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <ul> <li>Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to lead technical discussions with customers and partners and communicate risks/trade-offs clearly in an asynchronous environment.</li> <li>UK remote based role.</li> <li>Up to 50% travel at times.</li> <li>Demonstrated experience delivering two or more of the following consulting services: source code management migration, cloud architecture, DevOps engineering, or continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) consulting services.</li> <li>Enterprise software development experience, with the ability to translate requirements into clear technical designs and implementation plans.</li> <li>Progressive DevOps platform experience, including designing and implementing reliable, scalable systems with clear performance and security trade-offs.</li> <li>Hands-on experience deploying and managing infrastructure in cloud providers and on-premises environments, including using tools such as Terraform and Ansible.</li> <li>Ability to write clean, maintainable automation/integration code (e.g., Terraform modules, Ansible roles, scripts) and validate changes with appropriate testing and code review.</li> <li>Experience performing migrations to GitLab, including using Congregate or similar migration tooling.</li> <li>Working knowledge of data consistency and integrity concepts (e.g., ACID properties) and how they impact migration design and performance trade-offs.</li> <li>Strong problem-solving, decision-making, organizational, and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities with minimal supervision.</li> <li>Comfort working in a remote, asynchronous environment, using documented decisions (e.g., issues, proposals, and runbooks) to keep work unblocked across time zones while collaborating effectively across GitLab team members, partners, and customer stakeholders.</li> <li>Bachelor's Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or other advanced technical degree, or equivalent experience.              #LI-CM1</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Professional Services Technical Architect is part of GitLab's Professional Services organization. We partner with customers who are transitioning to GitLab, expanding how they use an existing GitLab installation, or planning complex upgrades to their infrastructure and processes. Our team brings a diverse set of skills across GitLab deployment, maintenance, and day-to-day usage, along with deep technical knowledge of adjacent tools and platforms. Working closely with Engagement Managers, partner consultants, and customer stakeholders, we focus on delivering high-quality outcomes, sharing best practices, and helping customers realize faster time to value from their GitLab investment. We operate in GitLab's remote, asynchronous environment and rely on clear documentation and transparent communication to collaborate effectively.</p> <p> </p> <p>This role models skills and behaviour aligned with GitLab Values and typically reports to the Regional Delivery Manager. title: Senior AI Engineer
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As an Senior AI Engineer at GitLab, you'll help build the foundation for GitLab's transformation into an AI-first company. Reporting to the Director, Enterprise AI, you'll be a hands-on technical leader responsible for delivering internal AI-powered solutions that drive measurable business outcomes.</p> <p>Building fast matters, but it's not enough on its own. This role starts with understanding the real problem: mapping how work moves across teams, tools, and handoffs, identifying the true constraint, and validating whether AI is the right solution before you begin development. From there, you'll take ownership from discovery through deployment, combining strong engineering skills with systems thinking and business understanding.</p> <p>Your initial focus will span Sales, Marketing, and Customer Support, where you will embed AI solutions into key systems and workflows. This role offers the opportunity to shape how GitLab team members work, improve flow across the organization, and help advance our mission in a remote, asynchronous, and values-driven environment.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Diagnose business problems before building solutions. Map workflows, identify constraints, and confirm whether AI is the right intervention. Be prepared to say "this doesn't need AI" when that's the honest answer.</li> <li>Own AI initiatives end-to-end, from stakeholder discovery and technical design through implementation, deployment, and iteration.</li> <li>Design, develop, and ship AI-powered solutions quickly, delivering working prototypes in days, not months, with a focus on practical outcomes and measurable business value.</li> <li>Improve organizational flow by building solutions that reduce bottlenecks, shorten lead times, and increase throughput. Measure success using flow metrics alongside adoption and ROI.</li> <li>Integrate AI capabilities into existing systems and workflows using APIs, orchestration tools, and modern AI platforms, including GitLab Duo Agent Platform, where appropriate. The right tool wins, whether that's custom code, a platform, or a well-crafted prompt.</li> <li>Be Customer Zero: leverage and showcase GitLab's AI offerings wherever possible, feeding real-world usage insights back to R&D.</li> <li>Partner closely with stakeholders across functions to understand the real constraints. Ask the right questions, bridge technical and non-technical perspectives, and align on outcomes before jumping to solutions.</li> <li>Define and track success through business metrics, flow metrics, and feedback loops that make performance visible and actionable.</li> <li>Contribute to technical direction by evaluating tools, documenting patterns, and creating reusable foundations that help the team scale its impact.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>A Technologist at Heart - </strong>Genuinely invested in technology, the foundational and the cutting-edge in equal measure. You're as energised by a well-designed API integration as you are by the latest foundation model release. You reach for the simplest solution that solves the problem well, rather than forcing new technology when proven approaches would do. AI is a powerful part of your toolkit, but it sits on top of solid engineering fundamentals, not in place of them.</li> <li><strong>Competent, Confident Coding Skills - </strong>You can build working solutions end-to-end, write clean and maintainable code, and debug effectively. Whether your skills were honed in a traditional engineering role, through building automations, or shipping side projects, what matters is that you can deliver production-quality work independently.</li> <li><strong>AI</strong><strong> & LLM </strong><strong>Technical Depth - </strong>Strong proficiency in at least one modern scripting language (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or similar) and a solid understanding of REST APIs, GraphQL, and integration patterns. Deep, practical experience with modern AI technologies, specifically: Prompt engineering as a core discipline: designing effective system prompts, managing context windows, structuring multi-turn interactions, evaluating output quality, and iterating systematically on prompt design.</li> <li><strong>Model selection and cost-performance trade-offs: </strong>understanding when a smaller fine-tuned model outperforms a general-purpose large one, when RAG is the right architecture versus expanding the context window, and how to make principled decisions about capability versus cost.</li> <li><strong>Agentic architecture patterns: </strong>tool use, multi-agent orchestration, human-in-the-loop designs, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and production-grade reliability patterns.Practical fluency across the LLM ecosystem: hands-on experience with models from Anthropic, OpenAI, open-source alternatives, and the judgment to know which to reach for and when.</li> <li><strong>AI Safety & Risk Awareness - </strong>You think critically about how the solutions you build could be exploited, misused, or produce unintended consequences. You know how to design appropriate guardrails (input validation, output filtering, access controls, prompt injection defences, and data leakage prevention) and you treat these as first-class engineering concerns.</li> <li><strong>Systems Thinking & Diagnostic Rigour - </strong>The ability to look at a complex process and see the constraint. Comfortable mapping how work flows end-to-end, identifying bottlenecks, and tracing problems to root causes before proposing solutions. You instinctively ask "what's actually blocking flow here?" before asking "what model should I use?"</li> <li><strong>Business System Expertise - </strong>Familiarity with the landscape of enterprise business systems, CRM (Salesforce), marketing automation (Marketo), support platforms (Zendesk), integration and orchestration tools (Workato), AI platforms (Relevance AI), and enterprise search and knowledge tools (Glean). You don't need deep experience with all of these, but to understand what they do, how they fit together, and be willing to build with and across them. A strong understanding of enterprise data models and workflows is essential.</li> <li><strong>Broad Functional Understanding - </strong>Ability to have meaningful conversations with stakeholders across diverse domains and quickly understand their unique needs.</li> <li><strong>End-to-End Ownership - </strong>Track record of owning complex initiatives from discovery through delivery. Comfortable operating with ambiguity and driving to measurable outcomes independently.</li> <li><strong>Product Mindset - </strong>Ability to scope MVPs, prioritise ruthlessly, and deliver iteratively. In addition, consider adoption, user experience, and business outcomes.</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>Preferred requirements</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with GitLab platform and CI/CD workflows</li> <li>Background in consulting, solutions engineering, or customer-facing technical roles</li> <li>Familiarity with value stream mapping, flow metrics, or Theory of Constraints thinking</li> <li>Experience with low-code/no-code orchestration tools (n8n, Make, Workato) alongside custom development</li> <li>Previous startup or high-growth company experience</li> <li>Experience mentoring or leading technical projects with junior engineers</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>You will join the Enterprise Technology & AI team. We're the backbone of the organisation, driving transformation in how GitLab team members make decisions, operate at scale, and deliver results for our customers.</p> <p>We believe the best AI solutions start with understanding the system, not the technology. We value people who think in constraints and flow, who build with conviction, and who never stop learning. We work in an all-remote, asynchronous setting, guided by GitLab's values of collaboration, results, efficiency, diversity, inclusion and belonging, iteration, and transparency.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. Success</a>, and <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/sales/">Sales</a> teams to drive bug fixes, influence feature development, and help shape product goals and roadmap.</li> value="6">Create and improve support content, including documentation and knowledge articles, to help customers and GitLab team members resolve issues more efficiently.</li> <li value="7">Partner Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As a Senior Backend Engineer on the Duo Chat team, focused on Chat Engine, you'll build the core AI capabilities behind GitLab Duo Chat, the natural-language and agentic interface to the GitLab DevSecOps platform. Much of your work will involve building flow components and agentic flows in the Flow Registry, the Python framework built on LangGraph within our Duo Workflow Service that powers agentic chat, and integrating them with the GitLab Rails monolith.</p> <p>You'll own complex backend features from start to finish across both services. You'll integrate large language models and orchestrate multi-agent flows so customers can work faster and more securely across the software development lifecycle. This work sits where GitLab's core platform meets its AI strategy, and reliability, performance, and answer quality directly shape the customer experience.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Design and build flow components and agentic flows in the Flow Registry using Python and LangGraph within the Duo Workflow Service. These reusable building blocks power agentic Duo Chat and, increasingly, other AI features across GitLab.</li> <li>Develop, ship, and maintain backend features for GitLab Duo Chat across the Python Duo Workflow Service and the GitLab Rails monolith in a secure, well-tested, and performant way.</li> <li>Integrate new generative AI models, providers, tools, and multi-agent orchestration patterns into Duo Chat to expand its capabilities and improve answer quality.</li> <li>Design, implement, and review GraphQL and Representational State Transfer (REST) application programming interfaces (APIs) and related monolith logic, including chat entry points, permissions, and foundational-flow registration. Keep contracts with frontend clients and host systems reliable and clear.</li> <li>Improve debugging, observability, and test coverage using pytest, RSpec, and related frameworks; track and improve latency, error rates, and test coverage so AI-powered chat workflows stay reliable at scale.</li> <li>Collaborate with Product, User Experience (UX), frontend, and AI specialists to refine requirements and deliver high-quality improvements through iteration.</li> <li>Document standards, patterns, and learnings with other engineers, raising the bar for safe AI integration and evidence-driven engineering.</li> <li>Participate in Tier 2 on-call rotations to troubleshoot production issues, contribute to root cause analysis, and strengthen resiliency.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Significant experience building and maintaining production Python backends, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous or long-running workloads.</li> <li>Practical experience designing and shipping AI-powered, agentic backend features, including large language model integration, tool or function calling, and multi-agent orchestration. You use sound judgment about large language model limitations and safe use in production.</li> <li>Working proficiency in Ruby on Rails, or a strong willingness to learn it. Duo Chat integrates deeply with the GitLab monolith for chat entry points, GraphQL, permissions, and flow registration, and most of GitLab's codebase is written in Ruby.</li> <li>Proficiency designing or extending REST or GraphQL APIs with attention to scalability, maintainability, and backward compatibility.</li> <li>Strong Structured Query Language (SQL) skills and familiarity with relational databases such as PostgreSQL, including efficient queries and data modeling.</li> <li>Ability to find, diagnose, and prevent performance and reliability problems at scale.</li> <li>Experience solving technical problems of high scope and complexity and advocating for quality, security, and performance improvements across your team.</li> <li>Openness to learning and collaborating in an async-first, distributed team, applying transferable skills from related technologies or domains. Hands-on experience with agent frameworks such as LangGraph or LangChain is a strong plus.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>We're part of GitLab's AI Engineering organization and own the AI-powered chat experience embedded across the GitLab platform. Chat Engine is the backend-focused team within the Duo Chat group.</p> <p>We're backend, frontend, and AI specialists working asynchronously across time zones, using issues, merge requests, and documentation as our main collaboration tools. Our focus is to expand generative and agentic AI capabilities, improve the performance and reliability of chat workflows, and strengthen the debugging and testing foundations that let us run AI features safely at scale.</p> <p>For more on how we work, see the <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/ai/duo-chat/">team handbook</a> page.</p> <div class="c-message_actions__container c-message__actions"> </div> <div><span style="font-size: xx-small;"><span style="color: white;">Remote-Global</span></span></div><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto">Flexible Paid Time Off </a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/inclusion/tmrg-tmag/">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave">Parental Leave</a> </li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. title: Senior Backend Engineer, Architecture Engineering: Nonlinear Productivity
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As a Senior Backend Engineer on GitLab's Nonlinear Productivity team, you'll find and remove friction across the software development lifecycle using reliable AI-powered automation — diagnosing problems like long review cycles, manual release steps, and brittle automation, then building the automation and process changes that resolve them for good.</p> <p>Some examples of the problems this team takes on:</p> <ul> <li>Cutting the time it takes to complete a good code review — one that still keeps a human in the loop — by half, using agentic solutions.</li> <li>Turning a manual, error-prone release step into an agentic workflow that catches its own mistakes before a human ever has to.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Identify sources of friction across GitLab's software development lifecycle and scope agentic solutions to address them, turning vague pain points into concrete, buildable proposals.</li> <li>Design and build reliable AI-powered systems that follow step-by-step workflows, use tools and safety checks, and correct errors before taking engineering action — the kind of output you can actually trust with real engineering decisions.</li> <li>Build and maintain evaluation tools that judge agent output on correctness, constraint compliance, and cost, not on whether it merely "seems to work."</li> <li>Work across GitLab's codebase as each problem requires, going wherever the friction actually is rather than staying inside one service or product area.</li> <li>Apply distributed systems judgment to identify generated code that may fail under concurrency, at scale, or across self-managed, dedicated, and multi-tenant deployments, catching failures before they reach customers.</li> <li>Collaborate with the India-based group, sharing roadmaps, findings, and reusable agent tooling</li> <li>Take ownership of a greenfield problem space from day one, helping shape a proven internal fix into a capability GitLab could offer customers externally, with your scope and impact free to grow as the team scales.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Hands-on experience building agentic or large language model-based systems — multi-step orchestration, tool use, guardrails, and recovery patterns — and making them reliable in production, not treated as one-off prompts or demonstrations.</li> <li>A track record of working autonomously in unfamiliar codebases, getting oriented quickly, and driving solutions through completion.</li> <li>Strong distributed systems knowledge, including coordination, consistency, idempotency, rate limiting, failure modes, and degradation under load.</li> <li>Proficiency in Go, Rust, or Python, in that order of team priority, and the ability to read and modify code in the other languages.</li> <li>Helpful experience includes shipping autonomous agents that complete real tasks from start to finish; improving build systems, release processes, review workflows, or other parts of the software development lifecycle; and working with globally distributed teams, large language model workload costs, or production constraints across on-premises, air-gapped, single-tenant, and software-as-a-service deployments.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>Nonlinear Productivity — shortened internally to "NLP," with no relation to natural language processing — is one of GitLab's newest teams: a strategic incubation group that reports into AI Platform leadership under the direct sponsorship of the CTO. You'll help teams across GitLab reason confidently about data architecture, placement, and lifecycle management, while proactively identifying saturation points in our GitLab.com infrastructure and driving corrective actions with partner teams. With the team's recent move into the Data Engineering organization, you'll also shape new scalability and data health features for self-managed customers, working hands-on with PostgreSQL and Ruby on Rails in a fully remote, highly collaborative environment.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li value="1"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/22105">Data Growth Controls (retention enforcement and data lifecycle management)</a></li> <li value="2"><a class="textLink" and iterate backend features and data frameworks that make it safe and efficient for GitLab teams to work with data at scale across SaaS and self-managed deployments.</li> <li value="2">Design and build data retention and lifecycle management frameworks, including retention policy enforcement, bulk data removal tooling, and automated identification of tables that need retention policies.</li> <li value="3">Build shift-left guardrails, such as static analysis checks and schema-change-time enforcement, that catch unsustainable data growth patterns before they reach production.</li> <li value="4">Collaborate closely with product management, UX, frontend, infrastructure, software delivery, and analytics teams to design and ship high-performing solutions</li> <li value="5">Review and improve database-related changes from other engineers and community contributors, ensuring data integrity, safety, and performance across all deployment scenarios.</li> <li value="6">Design, build, and maintain tooling such as SQL traffic replay and background operations frameworks to proactively surface and address scalability and performance issues.</li> <li value="7">Research, design, and implement improvements to data retention and lifecycle management, database performance, scalability, and data health, including areas like soft delete strategies and database migration testing.</li> <li value="8">Document database best practices, patterns to avoid, and data architecture guidance to enable developers to make informed decisions.</li> <li value="9">Develop proactive tooling and guardrails that help developers detect and remediate potential performance and data issues early in the development lifecycle.</li> <li value="10"> </li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Professional software engineering experience working with PostgreSQL in large, complex production environments, including high availability solutions with automatic failover and zero-downtime data migrations as well as managing large or fast-growing datasets through approaches such as data retention, archiving, partitioning, or lifecycle management.</li> <li value="2">Proficiency with Ruby on Rails or another Ruby framework, including designing, implementing, and reviewing backend features.</li> <li value="3">Ability to reason about software design, algorithms, and performance trade-offs at a system level.</li> <li value="4">Strong written communication skills and comfort working asynchronously in an all-remote, distributed team.</li> <li value="5">Self-directed work style with effective organizational skills and the ability to manage priorities as a "manager of one".</li> <li value="6">Alignment with GitLab's values, including transparency, collaboration, inclusion, and contribution to open source.</li> <li value="7">Openness to learning and applying new tools and approaches, including transferable experience from related data, infrastructure, or developer tooling domains.</li> <li value="8">Willingness to participate in our <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/database-excellence/#tier-2-on-call">tier 2 dabase on-call rotation</a> in your time zone.</li> </ul> <p>The <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/database-excellence/">Database Excellence Group</a> is a remote, agile backend team that builds and maintains the frameworks, patterns, and tooling that enable GitLab teams to work confidently with data at scale across all application datastores. As part of the broader Data Engineering organization, we focus on data scalability, health, and developer enablement for both GitLab.com and thousands of self-managed deployments, collaborating closely with infrastructure, software delivery, and analytics stages to ensure data changes are safe, performant, and compatible across diverse environments. design for distributed storage, Git repository management, performance, reliability, and scalability problems, using data and benchmarking to guide decisions.</li> <li>Partner with engineers and teams across GitLab, including Git, Infrastructure, Site Reliability Engineering, Dedicated, and customer-facing teams, to deliver cross-functional outcomes.</li> <li>Improve engineering practices through mentoring, documentation, knowledge sharing, design reviews, and constructive code reviews.</li> <li>Take operational ownership of the systems you work on, including incident response, post-incident improvements, capacity and performance analysis, and customer escalations.</li> <li>Identify opportunities to improve work beyond an individual change through automation, reusable designs, better dashboards, upstream contributions, and improvements to development and testing workflows.</li> <li>Respond to user emergencies, platform alerts, and support requests, including regular on-call duties.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Significant professional experience building, debugging, and optimizing distributed or highly available software systems in large-scale production environments.</li> <li>Experience owning complex projects end to end, including technical design, execution, rollout, and operational support.</li> <li>Strong systems design skills and the ability to reason about performance, failure modes, consistency, concurrency, capacity, and observability.</li> <li>A track record of influencing technical decisions and working effectively with stakeholders across teams and disciplines.</li> <li>Experience mentoring engineers, improving team practices, and raising the quality of designs, code, testing, and documentation.</li> <li>Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical concepts and make trade-offs clear.</li> <li>Professional experience with Go or another backend or systems language.</li> <li>Experience operating production systems, participating in incident response, and turning operational learnings into durable improvements.</li> <li>Experience with Ruby, Git internals, gRPC, or Git server infrastructure is highly desirable.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>The Gitaly team includes Backend Engineers who title: Senior Backend Engineer, Platform Readiness
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><p>GitLab features must ship successfully across four distinct deployment platforms—Self-Managed, Dedicated, Dedicated for Government, and GitLab.com. Today, developers routinely discover platform compatibility issues late in development, triggering costly rework, delays, and emergency escalations. The Platform Readiness team is building an internal developer tooling capability that embeds platform readiness intelligence directly into GitLab's software development lifecycle to solve this problem.</p> <p>As a Senior Backend Engineer on the newly established Platform Readiness team, you'll architect and evolve the systems that enable features to ship successfully across all platforms by automating the evaluation of platform readiness requirements and surfacing risks early. You'll be a technical anchor for the team, driving the evolution of platform readiness from manual, ad-hoc assessments toward intelligent, agentic automation. Your work will directly impact GitLab's ability to ship features faster while dramatically reducing the risk of platform-readiness gaps and the operational burden of cross-platform validation.</p> <p>You'll receive onboarding and technical guidance from other engineers and team leadership as you establish the technical direction for the Platform Readiness team.</p> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Contribute to the Platform Readiness team's agentic workflows</strong> on the Duo Agent Platform: design, implement, and evolve the Core Agentic Workflow (currently published to the AI Catalog as a DAP flow) and the Requirements Agent, enabling automated evaluation of platform readiness assessments against platform requirements</li> <li><strong>Evolve the platform requirements knowledge base</strong>: contribute to schema design, validation tooling, and CI systems that power the agentic workflow; ensure the schema captures the full scope of platform readiness concerns across all four platforms and domains</li> <li><strong>Build integration surfaces</strong> that enable feature teams to engage the Platform Readiness team where they already work: issues, merge requests, design documents, and CI/CD pipelines</li> <li><strong>Partner with platform teams</strong> (Infrastructure, Security, Data) to translate their expertise into structured platform requirements, domain skills, and validation logic without requiring specific domain knowledge</li> <li><strong>Contribute to the quality control feedback loop</strong>: design systems that surface assessment errors, missed gaps, and content drift back to the governance loop for continuous improvement; measure and improve assessment accuracy and guidance relevance</li> <li><strong>Mentor other engineers</strong> on the team in agentic-workflow standards, prompt discipline, evaluation methodology, and the principles of human-AI collaboration in platform readiness</li> <li><strong>Contribute to technical documentation and architectural decision records</strong> that document the Platform Readiness team's technical evolution and rationale for key design choices</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <h3>Required Experience & Skills</h3> <ul> <li><strong>5+ years of software engineering experience</strong> with at least 2+ years in backend, platform, or developer-facing tooling</li> <li><strong>Strong proficiency in TypeScript/Node, Python, or Golang</strong> (Ruby a plus)</li> <li><strong>Experience shipping developer-facing tooling</strong> where the primary user is another engineer</li> <li><strong>Understanding of GitLab-style development workflows</strong> (issues, epics, merge requests, CI/CD, code review) as first-class artifacts that automation can read and reason about</li> <li><strong>Ability to work in cross-functional environments</strong> across multiple platform teams</li> <li><strong>Experience with structured content systems, schemas, or validation tooling</strong></li> </ul> <h3>Highly Valued Experience</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Experience with AI/agentic systems</strong> (DAP, ADK, LangGraph, or similar) OR demonstrated ability to reason rigorously about the boundary between what AI should decide and what humans must own</li> <li><strong>Experience integrating with LLM APIs</strong> and reasoning about cost, latency, evaluation, and failure modes</li> <li><strong>Background in developer experience or platform engineering</strong></li> <li><strong>Experience with governance patterns</strong> for shared standards and cross-org decision-making</li> <li><strong>Open source contribution history</strong> in platform, developer experience, or AI infrastructure</li> <li><strong>PostgreSQL or other relational database experience</strong> at scale</li> </ul> <h3>What Makes You Stand Out (Strong Plus)</h3> <ul> <li>You've <strong>shipped agentic workflows in production</strong> and dealt with the operational complexities of AI-driven automation</li> <li>You have <strong>experience designing schema-driven content systems</strong> with non-engineer authors and evolving them as requirements change</li> <li>You've <strong>built developer platform teams at scale</strong> and understand the dynamics of enabling other engineers</li> <li>You have <strong>observability and monitoring experience for AI systems</strong>, including evaluation metrics, cost tracking, and failure analysis</li> <li>You can <strong>explain complex concepts</strong> (agentic workflows, platform readiness, governance) clearly to platform teams, feature teams, product managers, and executives</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Platform Readiness team is part of GitLab Developer Experience, building internal developer tooling capability for platform readiness across GitLab's four deployment targets: Self-Managed, Dedicated, Dedicated for Government, and GitLab.com. We partner with platform teams, feature teams, and product management to ensure every feature is evaluated against platform readiness requirements before it ships.</p> <p><strong>Current challenges we're tackling:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Moving from manual coordination to embedded automation:</strong> Transitioning from manual, ad-hoc platform readiness assessments to automated, agentic evaluation while maintaining human oversight and trust</li> <li><strong>Building a structured, machine-readable requirements body:</strong> Evolving the platform requirements schema to capture the full scope of platform readiness concerns across all domains and platforms</li> <li><strong>Making platform readiness native to the tools feature teams already use:</strong> Enabling platform teams to contribute domain expertise and validation logic without requiring deep Platform Readiness infrastructure knowledge</li> <li><strong>Building the measurement systems to know we're working:</strong> Creating observability and evaluation frameworks that give us confidence in agentic-workflow decisions and surface failures early</li> </ul> <p><strong>Team structure:</strong></p> <p>You'll be joining a newly established Platform Readiness team that is building the capability to embed platform readiness intelligence into the development lifecycle. resiliency.</li> <li value="8">Share knowledge through code review, technical documentation, and everyday collaboration while learning from others.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Professional experience with Vue.js or another modern JavaScript web framework, such as React, Angular, or Ember, and experience using GraphQL for application programming interface integration and data management.</li> <li value="2">A solid understanding of semantic hypertext markup language, cascading style sheets, core JavaScript concepts, responsive design, accessibility standards, and frontend performance best practices.</li> <li value="3">Experience solving complex policy, permissions, or rules-based problems in web applications and making that complexity feel simple and usable.</li> <li value="4">Experience writing frontend unit and acceptance tests with tools such as Jest, Karma, Jasmine, Mocha, ava, or tape, and familiarity with the testing pyramid.</li> <li value="5">A track record of raising the bar on how your team or group uses artificial intelligence coding agents in a large, complex monorepo, including scoping tasks, reviewing generated code, and knowing when to take direct control, paired with a clear view of where these tools fall short and how to work around it.</li> <li value="6">Experience using Git in a professional environment and familiarity with collaborative code review processes.</li> <li value="7">Clear written and spoken English communication skills, including the ability to influence without authority and share useful status updates in a remote, asynchronous environment.</li> <li value="8">The ability to manage priorities independently, work through ambiguity, take ownership, and seek guidance for decisions that are difficult to reverse.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The functional team works across Europe and North America, supporting both synchronous and asynchronous collaboration. It includes six engineers, with one frontend engineer today, so this role offers a meaningful opportunity to coach and mentor others and provide technical leadership in the frontend domain. We work closely with Code Review and Gitaly, alongside sibling teams covering Repository Sync & Interop, Source Code Experience, and Repository Scale, Performance & Git Infrastructure. We're maturing GitLab's branch protection offering while maintaining availability, reliability, and stability through bug fixes and focused technical debt work. project calls for it</li> <li>Contribute to technical direction for the systems you own, including making build-versus-buy suggestions and evaluating trade-offs between speed and long-term maintainability</li> <li>Identify and resolve performance, scalability, or reliability issues in backend systems before they become user-facing problems</li> <li>Review code and designs from other engineers, and provide feedback for peers</li> <li>Mentor junior engineers on the team</li> <li>Document system design decisions and backend architecture so other engineers can build on your work without you in the room</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <ul> <li>A strong track record of owning backend systems in production</li> <li>Strong fullstack technical skills with proficiency in Vue, Node, Go, and Ruby</li> <li>Deep experience with backend service design, including API design, data modeling, and database performance</li> <li>A track record of making sound technical trade-offs independently</li> <li>Comfort working in a fast-moving environment where priorities can shift with campaign or launch timelines</li> <li>Clear written communication skills, including architecture proposals and design records that help distributed teams make progress asynchronously.</li> <li>A practical and proactive approach to collaboration, with transferable experience welcomed from adjacent platform, data, or product engineering backgrounds.</li> </ul> <h2>Nice to have</h2> <ul> <li>Experience building systems for a marketing, growth, or GTM engineering context, such as web platforms, content tooling, or campaign infrastructure</li> <li>Experience working in a remote-first or distributed organization</li> <li>Experience mentoring other engineers and influencing technical direction beyond your own individual work</li> <li>Explaining those trade-offs clearly to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>GTM Engineering builds and operates This role sits at the intersection of cloud marketplace mechanics, hyperscaler funding, and systems administration, requiring someone equally comfortable setting GTM strategy, executing operationally, and leveraging AI to automate and scale hyperscaler processes.</p> <p>You will work closely with Systems, Revenue Technologies, Deal Desk, Enablement, Finance, and Legal to ensure GitLab's hyperscaler operations are accurate, scalable, and aligned to partnership objectives.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong>  </p> <p><strong>Marketplace Operational Strategy & Execution</strong></p> <ul> <li>Establish, oversee, and continuously improve end-to-end marketplace operational processes, including private offer management, CPPO/MCPO structures, and third-party integrations</li> <li>Serve as the internal expert on the private offer process end-to-end, partnering closely with Deal Desk to define, document, and iterate on workflows across AWS and GCP</li> <li>Own operational execution of hyperscaler funding initiatives such as AWS Strategic Collaboration Agreement (SCA), Marketplace Private Offer Partner Program (MPOPP), and GCP Marketplace Commit to Consume Program (MCCP), including milestone tracking, deal registration, claim workflows, and commit management</li> <li>Serve as the escalation point for marketplace and funding operations, resolving complex private offer, co-sell, and billing issues that span multiple systems or stakeholders</li> </ul> <p><strong>Technology Ownership & Administration</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as the primary relationship owner for the hyperscaler technology ecosystem, including Salesforce CRM partner objects, Tackle.io, and hyperscaler-specific PRM configurations</li> <li>Administer hyperscaler platforms, maintaining system health and data integrity across all hyperscaler-specific tools and integrations</li> <li>Co-manage vendor relationships, including Tackle.io and other marketplace tooling providers, covering roadmap engagement, renewal coordination, and SLA accountability</li> <li>Identify and build AI agents to automate repetitive hyperscaler workflows, such as offer status tracking, reporting, and co-sell registration, reducing manual effort and increasing operational throughput</li> <li>Partner with RevTech and Systems to maintain integration health across hyperscaler platforms, CRM, and downstream financial systems, including funding success tracking and reporting</li> </ul> <p><strong>Hyperscaler Funding Initiatives & Operational Management</strong></p> <ul> <li>Drive the operational strategy for hyperscaler funding initiatives across AWS and GCP, translating partnership objectives into co-sell and marketplace revenue plays</li> <li>Serve as the point of contact for hyperscaler partners and internal sales teams on funding operations, co-sell execution, utilization, and cross-functional escalations</li> <li>Identify opportunities to align hyperscaler funding with pipeline priorities and revenue goals</li> <li>Monitor funding performance across marketplace revenue, co-sell pipeline, and utilization; coordinate with Finance, AR, and Legal on billing and commitments</li> </ul> <p><strong>Process Design, Governance & Enablement</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, document, and govern end-to-end hyperscaler operational processes, including marketplace, co-sell, and funding initiatives, owning and maintaining the hyperscaler process map as the authoritative reference</li> <li>Continuously evaluate hyperscaler processes for AI automation opportunities, building and deploying agents that improve consistency, reduce cycle time, and scale operational capacity</li> <li>Drive gap remediation through cross-functional engagement with RSO peers and adjacent teams in IT, Finance, and Legal</li> <li>Build and maintain operational runbooks, process documentation, and training materials enabling consistent execution across all cross-functional partners</li> <li>Support configuration, testing, and maintenance of hyperscaler-facing and internal tools; document workflows and lead end-user training for field and operational teams</li> <li>Lead prioritization for hyperscaler system implementations, migrations, and platform enhancements with IT/Enterprise Applications</li> <li>Proactively surface process improvement opportunities and create GitLab Issues to advance the enhancement kickoff process</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></p> <ul> <li>6+ years of experience in cloud marketplace operations with direct ownership of hyperscaler-related workflows</li> <li>Hands-on experience with Tackle.io or equivalent cloud marketplace management platforms (AWS and GCP Marketplaces)</li> <li>Working knowledge of Salesforce CRM, including partner objects, opportunity management, and basic administration</li> <li>Deep familiarity with AWS and GCP marketplace mechanics, including private offer creation, CPPO/MCPO structures, co-sell registration, and billing and disbursement workflows</li> <li>Direct experience managing hyperscaler funding initiatives such as SCA, MPOPP, and MCCP, including strategy, operational execution, and compliance requirements</li> <li>Familiarity with hyperscaler co-sell operations, including AWS ACE and GCP Partner Advantage structures and operational requirements</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to design and document complex operational processes enabling consistent execution across distributed teams</li> <li>Hands-on experience working with AI tools and building agents to automate operational workflows; comfort evaluating processes for automation potential and translating them into working solutions</li> <li>Experience serving as an operational escalation point, resolving ambiguous issues that span systems, teams, and partner relationships</li> <li>Strong cross-functional instincts; you know how to align Deal Desk, IT, Finance, Legal, and Sales stakeholders around operational changes</li> <li>Experience with B2B SaaS channel or hyperscaler funding initiatives is a must</li> <li>Comfortable operating in a fast-moving, remote-first environment with a high degree of autonomy and a bias toward action</li> </ul> <h4><strong>How GitLab will support you</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a target="_blank">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/" target="_blank">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/" target="_blank">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave" target="_blank">Parental leave</a> </li> <li><a adoption and manage customer relationships across onboarding, adoption, business reviews, and renewals.</li> <li><strong>Knowledge</strong> of software development lifecycle practices, related tools,
